# week 10

- poisson regression
    - when you are bound by zero and can’t have any negative numbers
    - or have a lot of zeros
- predictive policing

    - racial bias reinforcement

### predictive policing model

- 2024 → future
- risk or predicted number of burglaries (spatially)
- grid-cell resolution level or police districts
- define number of crimes in each grid cell
- 500 ft
- grid function : fishnet ←
    - st_make_grid
    - cell_size in units of CRS (ft)
- OLS breaks
    - log the mean and not the data → poisson regression
- exp(B) the multiplicative change in expected count per one unit change in x
- one unit increase in x means 22% more expected burglaries
- poisson model assumes the **variance** is **equal** to the **mean**
- if the variance is not equal to the mean, model might be more of a negative binomial
- over dispersion: more zeros, may use negative binomial model
- Broken Windows Theory
- all feature types is 2024, the outcome is 2025
- K Nearest Neighbors compared to nearby cells
- each additional _ means _% more/fewer expected burglaries
